_comment: Single source of truth for the remote-control channel: protocol
constants, wire opcodes, marshalled struct layouts, and per-function
policies. gen_wire.py generates the C++ wire layer and the Python
protocol module from this table; nothing in those generated files is
hand-maintained. The same table is shaped to later emit SDK bindings.
Layout model: MSVC x64, little-endian. Scalars align to their size;
a struct aligns to its widest field and pads to that alignment. The
generated C++ static-asserts every described field offset and struct
size against the real headers, so a drift between this table and
Harken.h is a compile error, never a silent wire corruption.
Wire encodings. Command payload: u16 opcode, u16 reserved, then the
params in order. Reply payload: u16 opcode, u16 reserved, i32 VnResult,
then every scalar out param as u64; a fixed outstruct appends its
fields individually with no native padding, while an outrows param appends
ONE array section (u32 byteLength + raw row structs at the server's
row vintage) after the out params - the command carries only the
capacity, the server owns the buffer, and a capacity beyond the frame
budget is clamped (requiredCount still reports the full need, so the
clamp reads as an honest truncation). Strings: u32 byte length (0xFFFFFFFF
encodes a NULL pointer, 0 an empty string) + UTF-8 bytes, no NUL on
the wire. Descs: u32 declared structSize (0xFFFFFFFF encodes a NULL
desc pointer) + that many raw struct bytes (pointer fields zeroed) +
one out-of-line section per pointer field that lies within the
declared vintage, in field order; array sections carry u32 byteLength
+ bytes and must equal count*stride exactly. A declared vintage larger
than the server's compiled struct is passed through opaquely (no
section parsing, pointers stay null) so the engine's own
unknown-vintage refusal answers it.
Mirror exceptions, declared here so they are part of the table:
- VnConfig.onNotification (callback): not a wire command; the
remote server registers its own sink and forwards notifications
as advisory frames.
- Vn_CaptureSnapshot (pointer out-param): driven by the snapshot
subscription (Subscribe frame), not the command mirror; its
opcode exists but is refused with UseSubscription.
- Vn_Init / Vn_Term / Vn_Update / Vn_Suspend / Vn_Resume: the serving host owns the engine
lifecycle and the pump cadence; their opcodes are refused with
RefusedLifecycle.
- Vn_RegisterPCM / Vn_ReplacePCM: sample memory is process-local
and command frames never carry PCM blobs (the maxFrameBytes
rationale); remote content delivery is by host-local file path
(pack / stream surfaces). Refused with RefusedMemoryDesc.

VnConfig._comment: Not a wire desc (Vn_Init is refused-lifecycle); described here so the C# binding mirrors the full public struct and the layout asserts pin it. Callback/void* fields are raw C pointers (ptr:opaque) - 8 bytes, never wire-marshalled.

VnPCMDesc._comment: Not a wire desc (Vn_RegisterPCM / Vn_ReplacePCM are refused-memory-desc); described here for the C# binding and the layout pin. The two sample pointers are raw C pointers (ptr:opaque).

_comment: Public enums, result codes, and #define constants of Harken.h, transcribed
here so the C# binding generates them from this single table instead of
hand-copying them. gen_wire.py ignores this section entirely; only the C#
binding generator (gen_binding.py) reads it. Every value is drift-guarded:
gen_binding.py emits a C++ static_assert comparing each value against the
Harken.h symbol (compiled into harken_runtime_tests), so a mis-transcription here is
a compile error, not a silent binding bug.

callbacks._comment: C ABI callback function-pointer signatures (VnConfig.onNotification / .logCallback). Pointers marshal as IntPtr; the SDK layer decodes them. Cdecl, matching the extern-C engine exports.
